title: Dévissage des complexes ½ simpliciaux ∂ - parfaits et structures multiplicatives… (1975 ou 1976) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 40-42). Let C be the category of semi-simplicial k-modules L_* that are 'flasque and ∂-perfect': each is isomorphic to a finite direct sum of basic objects C^i_* (i ≥ 0). Let A ⊂ C be the full subcategory on the C^i_*. Grothendieck records the Hom spaces: Hom(C^i, C^j) = k·id for j = i, k·d_i for j = i+1, and 0 otherwise. In particular d_{i+1} d_i = 0. So A is the free k-linear category on a cochain complex, and C^• = (C^i, d_i) is the 'universal cochain complex'. C is the additive hull of A.

Prop 1 (previous page). For a k-additive category B, k-linear functors C → B correspond, by restriction to A, to k-linear functors A → B. These in turn correspond to cochain complexes in B, via F ↦ F(C^•).

This page, Example 1 (B = Ab_k, the k-modules). Yoneda gives a fully faithful functor α^• from C^op to cochain complexes of k-modules: L ↦ Hom_C(L, C^•) = (Hom(L, C^0) → Hom(L, C^1) → …).
- On the generators, α^•(C^i) = Hom(C^i, C^•) = K^i, the complex k --id--> k placed in degrees i and i+1, i.e. the contractible cone on k[-i].
- The map α^•(d^i) goes K^{i+1} → K^i (contravariance). It is the identity of k in degree i+1 and zero elsewhere, as in the drawn ladder diagram.
- Essential image: complexes isomorphic to finite sums of the K^i. These are bounded complexes of free finite-type modules that are acyclic, with cocycles free or direct factors of free modules. Over a local ring or a PID this is the same as bounded, contractible, free of finite type.

Example 2 (B = Ab_k^op). Using the contravariant represented functors M ↦ Hom_C(M, L), the same chain of equivalences (with Hom(C^op, Ab) ≅ Hom(C, Ab^op)^op, and complexes in Ab^op being the opposite of chain complexes) gives a second fully faithful functor β_•(L) = Hom(C^•, L). This is a chain complex …→ Hom(C^1, L) → Hom(C^0, L).
- Next page: β(C^i) = (k --id--> k) in degrees i and i-1, while β(C^0) = k in degree 0.
- So β lands in bounded chain complexes of free finite-type modules with H_i = 0 for i > 0 and H_0 free. This matches condition (b) of p. 40, 'π_i(L) = 0 for i > 0'. It strongly suggests β is the (Moore/normalized) chain complex of the semi-simplicial module.

Page 42 then relates α and β by k-duality: a perfect pairing Hom(C^n, x) × Hom(x, C^n) → k.

Purpose. This gives a linear-algebra model, an equivalence with explicit complexes, of the category of 'perfect' semi-simplicial modules. It feeds the dévissage of ∂-perfect semi-simplicial complexes and their multiplicative structures (cote 137).
errors: The phrase read as 'dont la restriction à C' should be 'restriction à A': the formulas given concern only the generators C^i of A.

The essential image of α is stated hesitantly. Strictly, finite sums of the K^i have free cocycles, whereas a bounded contractible complex of free finite-type modules only has projective cocycles. So equality of essential images needs k local or a PID, or 'stably free' to be handled. Grothendieck hedges on this in the margin of p. 40 ('on suppose … principal').
The target categories should be bounded complexes (finite sums). 'Libres de type fini en toutes dimensions' needs this boundedness added.
Variance notation for β is inconsistent: the diagram yields a covariant functor C → chain complexes Ab_{k*}, but the final line reads 'C° ↪ Ab_{k*}'. This is probably a slip or a misreading.

The stated Hom computation (Hom(C^i, C^j) nonzero only for j = i, i+1) is incompatible with C^i being the literal free module on the representable semi-simplicial set Δ^i, where Hom(k[Δ^i], k[Δ^j]) = k[Δ^j_i] is large. So the meaning of 'Δ̂^i ⊗ k' must be some non-representable 'flasque' object. This is not checkable from this page alone.

ideas.what: Additive functors out of the additive hull of the free k-linear category on a complex d²=0 are the same as cochain complexes in the target ('universal cochain complex' C^•)
ideas.modern_name: Complexes as k-linear functors from the 'walking complex' category (path category of the A_∞ quiver with relations d²=0); universal property of additive envelopes
ideas.usually_credited_to: Folklore in enriched/additive category theory (Mitchell, Kelly, Freyd-style additive Yoneda)

ideas.what: Additive Yoneda embedding of C^op (resp. C) into cochain (resp. chain) complexes of free k-modules, computing the generators as contractible cones K^i and β(C^0) = k
ideas.modern_name: Additive Yoneda lemma; contractible two-term complexes as indecomposable projective-injective summands

ideas.what: Description of 'perfect flasque' semi-simplicial k-modules as equivalent to bounded free complexes with homology only in degree 0 (a partial Dold–Kan for semi-simplicial objects without degeneracies)
ideas.modern_name: Dold–Kan-type correspondence for semi-simplicial (Δ_inj) modules restricted to a subcategory
ideas.usually_credited_to: Dold–Kan (1958) for simplicial modules; semi-simplicial analogues scattered (e.g. Rourke–Sanderson for Δ-sets, not linear)

ideas.what: The two embeddings α (cochains, via Hom(-, C^•)) and β (chains, via Hom(C^•, -)) are exchanged by k-duality (Prop 2, next page)
ideas.modern_name: Duality between representable and corepresentable additive functors / perfect pairing

missed.claim: The page sets up an explicit linear model, via universal complexes, for a class of semi-simplicial k-modules ('∂-parfaits', rank polynomial in n). The model is meant to support a dévissage and multiplicative structures. A systematic theory of 'polynomial-rank flasque semi-simplicial modules' and its multiplicative structures does not seem to appear in the literature. Its eventual application is not visible on this page.
missed.quote: C^•_* = (C^i_*, T_*1) est un complexe de cochaînes … il joue le rôle du complexe de cochaînes universel
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Semi-simplicial objects (no degeneracies) appear in homotopy type theory and ∞-category foundations, where Dold–Kan fails. Partial linear models of this kind are of minor interest there, but the content of this page itself is routine additive Yoneda.

deep.surprise_reason: The page's mathematics is a careful but standard additive-Yoneda computation: complexes as functors out of the universal complex, giving contractible cones K^i. The only mildly interesting aspect is its use as a partial Dold–Kan model for a special class of semi-simplicial modules, part of an unpublished project.
transcription_corrections: 'et dont la restriction à C est donnée par' should probably read 'restriction à A'.
The ladder diagram shows α(C^i) with k in degrees i and i+1, and α(C^{i+1}) with k in degrees i+1 and i+2. The map α(d^i) points from α(C^{i+1}) to α(C^i), with id in degree i+1.

The essential-image passage reads roughly: 'L'image essentielle de C° est la catégorie des K^• ∈ Ob Ab_k^{•*} qui sont libres de type fini en toutes dimensions, et qui sont à cohomologie nulle (cocycles facteurs directs d'un libre de t.f.) et itou'. The parenthetical is uncertain.
Ex 2: 'qui est k-linéaire (k commutatif)'; the left margin note reads 'commentaire pour Ex 2'.
The final line is probably 'C ↪^{β_•} Ab_{k*}' (covariant, chain complexes) rather than 'C°'.
